Instrumentation

 Inter Discipline Check: 5 Disciplines Engineers Coordinate

 A P&ID that looks perfect on paper can still send a project back for rework.

 This review step catches that before a single cable is pulled or a single nozzle is welded.

 
 Inter Discipline Check 
 IDC 
 P&ID Review 
 EPC Engineering 
 




 Inter Discipline Check makes sure design output from one engineering department actually works for every other department that has to build around it.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn Inter Discipline Check, the review step that lines up process, mechanical, piping, civil and electrical design before construction begins.


 We will cover what each discipline checks, the documents involved, who performs the review, and why skipping it gets expensive fast.


 
 
 
 What Is Inter Discipline Check


 Inter Discipline Check, usually shortened to IDC, is a formal review step where every engineering discipline on a project checks its own design output against the documents produced by every other discipline.


 The goal is simple. A P&ID drawn by the process team, a layout drawn by the piping team, and a cable schedule drawn by the electrical team all have to describe the same physical plant. IDC is where a design engineer confirms they actually do.


 This review happens before drawings are issued for construction, since a conflict caught on paper costs far less than the same conflict caught on site with a crane already in place.


 
 Did You Know

 IDC is sometimes called a squad check in EPC contracts. Both names describe the same review, engineers from every discipline sitting together and checking one drawing set against another before it gets issued.




 
 
 Advertisement 


 
 


 5 Disciplines an Inter Discipline Check Covers


 A real IDC touches every discipline that has to physically build around the same equipment, so each one reviews a different slice of the same design.


 
 
 1

 Process and Chemical

 Reviews the P&ID itself, instrument legend, process connection sizes, signal types, and which instruments belong to a vendor package versus the main plant.

 

 
 2

 Mechanical

 Reviews vendor package specifications, PLC and HMI preferences, control panel enclosure material, and the cabling inside a skid.

 

 
 3

 Piping

 Reviews the 3D model for instrument connection details, cable tray routing on pipe racks, and alignment with hookup drawings.

 

 
 4

 Civil and Structural

 Reviews layout drawings for wall and floor cutouts, since cable routes have to physically pass through a structure that civil already designed.

 

 
 5

 Electrical

 Reviews the load list against the P&ID for motor quantity, signal considerations for I/O lists, cable tray layout, and earth pit placement.
